title: Lior and the Hollow
premise: Casper Joubert has spent her whole life in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot follow, hiding the beast-speech that would see her burned. When a royal hunt for the gifted breaches the valley's borders and captures her brother-figure, an old badger she can actually understand, Casper is dragged into a kingdom unraveling under a king possessed by something ancient wearing his crown. Guided by a disgraced hunt-captain ordered to kill her and a runaway court mage who knows too much, she discovers her gift is not random: beasts remember the king's true voice, buried beneath the thing that stole it. To save them all, Casper must speak with every creature in the realm at once on the thirteenth full moon, unbinding the king even though doing so will strip away her own magic forever — and force her to choose between the duty of silence and the family she never expected to find.
about_author: Quentin Underhill is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to animals and claims it changed how he hears people. He writes fantasy about quiet gifts and loud worlds from a farmhouse surrounded by opinionated geese.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She tends goats and secretly trades gossip with a lame old badger named Bracken, establishing the valley's magic-dead peace and her hidden gift. Beat: cozy loneliness — belonging everywhere, known by no one.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Mill
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A royal crier announces the Gifted Hunt: all beast-speakers to be taken for questioning by the crown. The valley elders pledge cooperation. Beat: dread arriving in broad daylight.

chapters.title: Bracken Speaks Too Much
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Bracken warns her the Hunt uses hounds that smell magic even here, and begs her to run. She refuses to abandon him. Beat: stubborn love over self-preservation.

chapters.title: Hounds at the Treeline
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Hunt-captain Elara Voss leads riders into the valley; the hounds circle Casper's farm but cannot scent her — the valley shields her. They take Bracken instead when he attacks to cover her escape. Beat: guilt ignites the plot.

chapters.title: The Bargain with Voss
chapters.summary: Casper surrenders herself to Elara privately, offering information on other gifted in exchange for Bracken's life. Elara, disgusted by the Hunt's methods, hesitates. Beat: two enemies recognizing each other's honor.

chapters.title: Chains and Cages
chapters.summary: Elara's POV. Marching the prisoner convoy toward the capital, Elara watches interrogators torture a gifted child and begins quietly sabotaging orders. Casper witnesses it. Beat: moral fracture inside the machine.

chapters.title: The Mage in the Wagon
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Among the prisoners is Sef, a runaway court mage who recognizes what Casper is and whispers that the king hasn't spoken his own words in three years. Beat: the personal story opens onto the political one.

chapters.title: Night Escape
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Elara frees Casper, Sef, and the child during a storm, burning her own career to do it. Bracken is left behind in the capital's menagerie. Beat: found family forged in flight.

chapters.title: What the Wolves Know
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Fleeing through wild country, she speaks with a wolf pack and learns the king's hunters aren't hunting the gifted — they're searching for someone whose voice can reach the king. Her. Beat: she is the quarry and the cure.

chapters.title: Sef's Confession
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. He reveals he served the court mage who bound the king's true voice away to stop a war, and that the binding is failing — the thing wearing the crown grows stronger each moon. Beat: exposition becomes betrayal; Sef helped do it.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Elara's POV. She decodes her old military orders: on the thirteenth full moon, the 'coronation renewal' will make the possession permanent. They have until then. Beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Sanctuary of the Rootbound
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The fugitives shelter with a hidden community of gifted living in an ancient forest, led by a blind woman who hears through trees. Casper glimpses the family she could have had. Beat: hope, and the temptation to hide forever.

chapters.title: The Child Who Wouldn't Speak
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The rescued child, Mirei, is traumatized mute; Casper coaxes her back using animal signs, becoming an unwilling mentor. Beat: tenderness as strength; Casper stops running from responsibility.

chapters.title: Riders on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Elara's POV. Her former lieutenant, Dain, tracks them with a new weapon: a bell that screams in magic's frequency. The sanctuary must scatter. Beat: safety was always borrowed.

chapters.title: Bracken, Alive
chapters.summary: Casper's POV via a passing raven's memory: Bracken lives, caged in the royal menagerie as bait. The enemy knows exactly how to lure her. Beat: love weaponized against her.

chapters.title: The Road to the Capital
chapters.summary: Group decision scene, alternating voices. Against Sef's warnings, they choose to go to the capital before the thirteenth moon rather than flee. Beat: choosing the hard right over the easy wrong.

chapters.title: City of Bells
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Disguised as Elara's captured prize, Casper enters the capital and feels, for the first time, the hum of a thousand caged and working animals — a chorus waiting for a voice. Beat: awe and horror entwined.

chapters.title: The Menagerie at Midnight
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She reaches Bracken's cage; he is aged and half-mad, but lucid enough to tell her the king visits the animals at night, whispering, listening for an answer no beast dares give. Beat: reunion shadowed by revelation.

chapters.title: Audience with the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Caught by guards, she is brought before King Aldric — and the thing inside him goes still, tasting her gift. It offers her a place at its side. Beat: seduction of power; the villain speaks kindly.

chapters.title: The Voice Beneath
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In the king's presence she hears it: a faint human voice under the crown-thing's resonance, begging. Aldric is alive in there. Beat: the mission becomes mercy.

chapters.title: Elara's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Elara's POV. Dragged before the Hunt tribunal she once served, Elara faces Dain, her protégé, who offers her reinstatement if she delivers Casper. Beat: duty versus conscience made literal.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: Elara's POV. Elara publicly denounces the Hunt, is branded traitor, and escapes with wounds and Mirei, whom she swore to protect. Beat: she loses everything except what matters.

chapters.title: Sewers and Sparrows
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Hiding in the undercity, Casper recruits the city's sparrows, rats, and stray dogs into a spy network, mapping the palace for the thirteenth moon. Beat: the hunted become the intelligence corps.

chapters.title: Sef's Return to the Tower
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef infiltrates the mage tower to steal the original binding ritual and confronts his old master, who reveals the binding was meant to be temporary — and reversible only by a voice the king trusts. Beat: the plan crystallizes and narrows.

chapters.title: A Voice the King Trusts
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The riddle resolves: the king trusted no courtier — but he loved the royal stables' old mare, now dying, who remembers his real laugh. Casper learns the king's true name-song from her. Beat: grief and key turning together.

chapters.title: Dain's Choice
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Ordered to execute captured gifted children, Dain finds Elara's abandoned badge among their effects and defects, bringing the bell-weapon's weakness. Beat: even the loyal can turn; the family widens.

chapters.title: The Bell That Screams
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Using Dain's knowledge, they sabotage the great bells that suppress magic in the capital — but the act exposes their hideout. Beat: victory purchased with exposure.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Rookery
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. One sanctuary refugee, terrified, sells their location to the crown. Soldiers swarm; Bracken, smuggled out earlier, dies holding the tunnel open so the others escape. Beat: devastating loss; the price of the cause.

chapters.title: Grief Is a Country
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Broken by Bracken's death, Casper wants to quit; Mirei, speaking her first full sentence, tells her the animals are already gathering because they believe in her. Beat: the darkest hour answered by the smallest voice.

chapters.title: The Gathering
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. Across the kingdom, wolves, horses, ravens, and cattle begin moving toward the capital on instinct older than language. Elara rallies sympathetic soldiers; Sef prepares the counter-ritual. Beat: the tide turns visible.

chapters.title: Twelfth Moon Vigil
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. On the eve, Casper and Elara admit what they've become to each other — not quite love, deeper than friendship, a vow. Beat: stillness before the storm; love named aloud.

chapters.title: The Coronation Renewal
chapters.summary: Elara's POV. The thirteenth moon rises; the court assembles for the ritual that will seal the king forever. Elara walks into the cathedral openly, buying time by surrendering. Beat: sacrifice as strategy.

chapters.title: Every Beast at Once
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Standing in the packed square, Casper opens her gift fully and speaks with every creature in the realm simultaneously — overwhelming, nearly fatal, beautiful. Beat: climax begins; the small girl becomes the loudest voice alive.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Channeling the mare's name-song through ten thousand throats, she tears the crown-thing's hold loose while Sef unravels the binding below. The entity shrieks out of the king. Beat: climax peaks; magic burns out of her as she succeeds.

chapters.title: The Thing Without a Crown
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. The disembodied entity, starving, tries to seize Mirei; the gathered beasts and redeemed Dain drive it into the deep forest where the rootbound bind it in living wood. Beat: the villain denied even death's drama.

chapters.title: A King Made Human
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Aldric wakes hollowed and mortal, hearing for the first time what his kingdom suffered. He kneels to Casper publicly and repeals the Hunt. Beat: accountability; power humbled.

chapters.title: Silence Where the Song Was
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper wakes to a world gone quiet — her gift is gone, as the unbinding demanded. She grieves it like a limb. Beat: the cost made intimate.

chapters.title: Learning to Listen Again
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Weeks later, Casper discovers she doesn't need magic anymore: years of listening taught her to read animals — and people — with plain attention. Mirei, now her ward, shows first signs of a gift of her own. Beat: loss transmuted into wisdom.

chapters.title: The Valley Remembers
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. The company travels home: Elara offered a generalship she declines, Sef rebuilding the mage tower honestly, Dain farming. The valley, no longer needing to forget magic, welcomes them. Beat: home redefined as people, not place.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn Complete
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. One year later, on the anniversary moon, Casper sits on her hillside with her found family as a wild badger — Bracken's kin — settles beside her without a word needed. Beat: resolution; love against duty resolved into love fulfilled.
